title: NOR Universal Logic Gate (IC 7402)
summary: A NOR gate (NOT-OR) is a universal logic gate that produces a HIGH (1) output IF AND ONLY IF all inputs are LOW (0). Note that IC 7402 has a different pin layout compared to other 7400-series ICs.

working_principle: The NOR gate evaluates (A + B)'. If either input is 1, the output is 0. The output is 1 only when both A and B are 0. Note: In IC 7402, Pin 1 is 1Y (Output), while Pins 2 (1A) and 3 (1B) are Inputs!
applications: Buses Control Lines and Memory Decoding
advantages: High noise immunity in CMOS variants (74HC02)
disadvantages: Unique Pinout in IC 7402 (Output on Pin 1, Inputs on Pins 2 and 3) often trips up students!
common_mistakes: Wiring IC 7402 assuming Pin 1 and 2 are inputs (In 7402, Pin 1 is OUTPUT, Pins 2 & 3 are INPUTS!).
Confusing NOR truth table with NAND truth table.
quick_notes: IC 7402 Pinout Warning: Gate 1 Output is Pin 1, Inputs are Pins 2 & 3!
Pin 14 is VCC (+5V), Pin 7 is GND.
Tying both inputs of a NOR gate together forms a NOT Inverter.

viva_questions.q: What is special about the pin layout of IC 7402 compared to IC 7408 or IC 7432?
viva_questions.a: In IC 7402, Pin 1 is the Output, while Pins 2 and 3 are the Inputs. In 7408/7432, Pins 1 and 2 are Inputs, Pin 3 is Output.

viva_questions.q: How do you build a NOT gate from a NOR gate?

interview_questions.q: How many NOR gates are required to build an AND gate?
interview_questions.a: 3 NOR gates (Invert A using NOR, Invert B using NOR, then pass both into third NOR gate: (A'+B')' = A · B).
